Class MKCSlotProjection

java.lang.Object
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.MKCSlotProjection
public final class MKCSlotProjection extends Object
Projects InventoryMenu-bound slots onto foreign menus — chests, furnaces, donkeys, any AbstractContainerMenu — so a registered slot a consumer registered for the player inventory also appears, clicks, and syncs on a container screen. The second leg of inventory-screen parity, past "every screen whose menu already carries the slot" to "every screen that shows the player inventory."

The §0019 line this deliberately crosses

MKCSlots ships no registry on purpose: for the player's own InventoryMenu the consumer owns the <init> mixin, so the library injects nothing. Foreign menus have no such consumer-owned per-menu seam — AbstractContainerMenu's constructor doesn't carry the player, and mixing every (incl. modded) menu class isn't generic. To cover them the library must own a player-lifecycle seam (ServerPlayer.initMenu server-side, ScreenEvents.AFTER_INIT client-side) and therefore a registry of what to project. This is the one platform-shaped primitive, kept as narrow as possible: a registry of slot factories the library merely invokes (data + a deterministic build function), never a behavior callback that decides interaction semantics. The slots it builds are ordinary MKCSlots, so render / click→Storage / creative / sync all ride the same vanilla-slot paths the InventoryMenu slot already uses — the library adds a slot type to a foreign menu's list, it invents no behavior.

Sync safety — the load-bearing contract

The slots must appear on the server menu and the client menu with an identical set and order, established before the menu's first content sync, or remoteSlots/broadcastChanges desync (item flicker/dupe). Both seams therefore call this one appendProjectedSlots(AbstractContainerMenu, Player) against the same registry:
  • server: ServerPlayer.initMenu HEAD — runs after createMenu but before initMenu sends the initial ContainerSetContent, so that packet already includes the slots;
  • client: ScreenEvents.AFTER_INIT — fires synchronously inside handleOpenScreen, before the content packet is processed, so the client menu carries the slots when it arrives.
Because both sides iterate the same registered sources in the same order and each source's factory builds the same slot (same player-attached Storage size, same layout), the appended tail blocks are byte-identical. Registry order, reveal-predicate symmetry, and storage-size symmetry are the invariants to keep.

Relationship to the rest of the kit

Projection only puts the slots on the foreign menu. Drawing them is the panel pipeline (each slot is a SlotElement on its MKCContainerPanel, which renders inline on whatever screen its parity matcher accepts); shift-click into them is MKCSlotQuickMove; creative placement is the (now menu-general) creative-set-slot bridge. A consumer that wants pockets on a chest registers a projection source here and widens its panel's parity targeting to that screen.

  • Method Details

    • register

      public static void register(Predicate<net.minecraft.world.inventory.AbstractContainerMenu> appliesTo, MKCSlotProjection.ProjectionFactory factory)
      Registers a projection source: project the slot built by factory onto every opened menu appliesTo accepts. Call once at mod init.

      Both appliesTo and factory MUST evaluate identically on the logical server and the client (predicate on menu class/type/synced content; factory over a player-attached Storage) — see the sync-safety note in the class doc. Opt-in per slot: a slot that should stay inventory-only simply isn't registered here.

    • appendProjectedSlots

      public static void appendProjectedSlots(net.minecraft.world.inventory.AbstractContainerMenu menu, net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player)
      Appends every matching projected slot onto menu. Invoked by the library's server (initMenu HEAD) and client (AFTER_INIT) seams; idempotent per menu instance. No-op when no source matches (so the player's own InventoryMenu, never registered here, is untouched).
